# The driver seals a clean merge straight into %A, but only when it can be sure
# who to encrypt to. If access to the secret changed on both sides, ours' log is
# not that authority any more - sealing from it would use a stale recipient set.
# The seal is then left to the finalize, which has the merged log.

sesam-repo admin base.txt ours.txt theirs.txt

exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec sesam tell --user carol --recipient $CAROL_PUBKEY --group ops
cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add s'

# THEIRS grants dev and edits the secret.
exec git checkout -b topic
exec sesam add s --group-add dev
cp $TMPDIR/theirs.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs: dev only'

# OURS grants ops instead, and edits a different line.
exec git checkout master
exec sesam add s --group-add ops
cp $TMPDIR/ours.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: ops only'

# The line edits do not overlap, so the content merges cleanly - but the
# recipient sets disagree, so the driver declines to seal rather than guess.
! exec git merge topic
stderr 'access to it changed on both sides'
stderr 'sealed with the merged recipients when you commit'
! stderr 'could not be resealed'

# The finalize does it, and the result verifies.
exec git commit --no-edit
exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'OURS'
stdout 'THEIRS'

-- base.txt --
first = BASE
middle = BASE
last = BASE
-- ours.txt --
first = OURS
middle = BASE
last = BASE
-- theirs.txt --
first = BASE
middle = BASE
last = THEIRS
